groups.instruction: Answer the questions below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A lecturer reports a problem with her university laptop.

transcript.text: IT helpdesk, Sam speaking. How can I help?
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Hello Sam. I'm having trouble with my university laptop, and I need to report it.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: No problem. It's one of the most common reports we receive this term, so I'm sure we can fix it.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: I hope so, because I use it for all my lectures.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Sure. Let me log it. Could I have your surname, please?
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: It's Hughes, H-U-G-H-E-S. I'm in the Geography department.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Thanks, Dr Hughes. And what exactly is the problem?
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: The screen keeps turning off after a few minutes, even when I'm working. At first I thought it was the battery, but it's the same when it's plugged in.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: That sounds like a power setting problem, or possibly a loose cable inside the laptop.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: I did try restarting it several times, and I updated the software last week, but nothing changed.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: I see. Could you give me the serial number? It's on a sticker on the bottom of the laptop.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Let me look. It's X-T-4-Q.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: X-T-4-Q. Got it. And where are you at the moment?
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: In my office, which is room two-fourteen on the second floor of the Science Building.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: That's the new wing of the building, isn't it? I was there last week fixing a printer.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Yes, it's quite far from the main entrance, so it's not easy to get to.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Okay. We'll need to take the laptop for repair. Before that, have you saved your files?
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Not everything. I've got my lecture slides on the desktop, but nothing is in the cloud.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Then please back up your documents first. You can use the university cloud, or a memory stick if you prefer.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: I'll use the cloud. How long will the repair take?
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Usually about three days, but if we have to order a part, it can take a week.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Three days isn't too bad. I just need it for the weekend to prepare some marking.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: I understand. We'll try to prioritise it, because we know lecturers need their equipment.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: I have a lecture on Monday. Is there any way to borrow another laptop?
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Yes, we have loan laptops. You can collect one from the help desk on the first floor of the library. Bring your staff card.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Will it be ready by Thursday?
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: The loan one will be ready tomorrow, and I expect your own to be repaired by Thursday, but I'll send you an email to confirm.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Wonderful. And do I need to bring the charger as well?
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: Yes, please bring the charger. Without it we can't test the battery properly.
transcript.speaker: SAM

transcript.text: Thank you, Sam. You've been very helpful.
transcript.speaker: NINA

transcript.text: You're welcome. Have a good day, Dr Hughes.
transcript.speaker: SAM
